Can we normalize playing Minecraft how you want?

I’ve seen countless videos on trying to nerf or get rid of items that are optional and these ideas kind of limit creativity in a game that prioritizes being able to do whatever you want. Like when I saw a video of someone who wanted totems to not be a renewable source and to only be found in strongholds. Which kind of messes up the lore and stumps the creativity of farms. Also, mods. I’ve seen people say that Fulbright is cheating or cheating that people with vision problems should only use them.
it just makes no sense to me on how someone could dictate how someone plays a game that markets its self as a free play game. This game is also $30 so getting to do whatever I want is a bottom line. You know what I mean?
Edit: I feel like I should clear things up because I don’t think I worded this correctly. What I meant was for people to play how they want and to no project how they play to be correct or to label things as cheating. I didn’t go over balance but I feel like if we balanced certain things with others should be that the lesser options get a buff. Rules change when you do content or run a server. But I hope we can all agree that quality of life mods aren’t cheating. Even though they are mods. Y‘know?

I wish mojang would just take a risk once in a while.

I’m tired of witnessing the creativity of minecraft dungeons just to see none of it get added to vanilla. So many cool concepts and not a single one will ever touch vanilla.
The player base has been begging for a fourth dimension since the End was added. However, mojang is way too cautious about any additions that they end up just adding the safest possible feature. Its why every new content drop is retextured wood or additional colors to the building palate. Which dont get me wrong, is great, but also just more
horizontal bloating when the vertical progression has not significantly changed in 15 years.
We want an end update, a new boss, a new dimension, more late game progression. Every recent drop feels like its being built for creative mode and not survival. I want to see genuine challenge added to this game. In a perfect world, minecraft’s difficulty would progress as you advance further instead of the player just growing stronger with no legitimate threats other than bad timing.
I know the game is a one time purchase and gets continuously updated for free. I know theres a million free mods out there as well. But if the game is going to be updated, they might as well add something significant.

Who else never uses the elytra?

First of all, I fully respect and appreciate that most players love the elytra, so it obviously shouldn’t be removed from the game.

But I’ve been playing since 2012, and I’ve never touched the elytra.

I just know that it would instantly make my gameplay experience worse.
First of all, it largely takes the “survival” out of survival Minecraft, in my opinion. Dangerous terrain? Just fly over it. Surrounded by mobs? Just fly away. Fall from a cliff? No problem—you can fly. And when you then add automatic farms and shulker boxes, aren’t you just playing Creative with extra steps?
The biggest issue for me, however, is that it takes all the intrinsic motivation out of building infrastructure.
I love building infrastructure. I don’t just want to build pretty things; I want to build functional things that expand my horizons: railroads, bridges, tunnels, horse infrastructure, harbors, nether hubs, ender pearl cannons.
The elytra negates the functionality of pretty much all of that.
I know some will say it’s an “endgame item.” But my games don’t end after beating the dragon. Why should my “end-game” be less fun than early/mid game. I always have lots more to do, including things that are much more advanced than beating the Ender Dragon. Are those things easier with an elytra? Yes. They would also be easier in Creative mode, but they would be a hell of a lot less fun to accomplish, in my opinion.
But I’m clearly in the minority on this. I’m just interested to hear from others like me, and also to hear if anyone has arguments for why I should give the elytra a chance.

Friendly reminder that Minecraft is a sandbox survival, not a progression rpg

Saw the trailer of RealismCraft recently and so many people were commenting “Minecraft if Mojang cared” and “So just Minecraft but better?” No hate to the mod or mods like this in general but I’m so sick of people who think this is better Minecraft. Minecraft can definitely be improved but this isn’t it.
The focus of Minecraft has never been bosses and weaponry and progression, but people act like it is. Doing things like given every mob and action animations like this will hurt performance on lower end PCs and restrict the scale of larger red stone builds because of all the entities they tend to process. In fact a lot of the changes people suggest will “improve” Minecraft hurt the red stone and building community.
Even things like making 12 unique eyes required to reach the end will increase rng and greatly extend the time needed to reach the end which would be great for people who want the ender dragon to feel more final bossy but really hurt people who just want purpur and shulker shells and elytra for their builds as soon as possible.
Again, I’m not saying Minecraft can’t be improved, but it is NOT an rpg. It’s a sandbox survival. Y’all need to keep all the communities of this game in mind when you suggest your “improvements”.

My boyfriend on the other hand CANNOT play Minecraft the way I do, it’s caused real arguments and bust been tedious, I get way too stressed when I think I’m gonna lose everything I worked for and I get lost too easily even with coordinates.
I’ve tried playing with him where we do it his way for a little bit then play mine for a little bit but when it came to play it my way he said “no, it’s just not fun for me and I’m not going to play it that way because it’s dumb” he used so mean words to describe the people who play it this way.
He explained to me that the achievements is the best thing about the game and if he can’t have the award of doing something why do it? I told him that I just want to have fun and build stuff with him and that keep inventory can still be challenging and rewarding even without achievements in the game.
I wish Minecraft had better settings where he could get achievements and I can play how I want. So then we can at least play together, or a setting where when you die you keep some of the stuff but it’s random, like the first 3 things in your tool bar are the only things you keep etc and you lose everything else.

"Items are intended to be impermanent"

Recently Jeb tweeted on Bluesky, answering a question about anvil level cap. He said "All items are meant to be impermanent".

I know that social media posts shouldn't be taken as gospel, even from the game's lead designer. But I want to address an big issue which affects the game directly.
Losing items or death or tools breaking always was part of Minecraft, yes. One issue, times done changed. In old version of Minecraft, progression was much simpler, and once you have diamonds you're essentially done. In modern versions, it takes HOURS to get to the most optimal gear, with a lot of grind.
On itself it's not bad, but if you lose gear in Beta Minecraft, you're set back by 30 minutes of mining diamonds. If you lose gear in modern Minecraft, you lose potentially hours of grind - mining netherite, getting XP, grinding for emeralds... You technically don't need the best items, but they can save a lot of time with building or exploring. And the whole point of progression is to progress -_-
Mojang might not know what they're doing. They barely address this issue, but at least they won't make it worse by removing Mending, which is an necessary evil. Alongside Gravestone mods/plugins or keepinventory gamerule...

I don't get people's beef with Copper...

People say Copper is worthless since it's not as good as Iron and you can find Iron pretty easily and fast.

And while they are not wrong, from my experience, Iron is harder to find and you need to save up for quite some time before you have enough to craft a full set of Iron equipment.

Copper by contrast is almost as plentiful as Coal, after a few minutes I always have WAY more Copper than I know what to do with.
You need at least 34 Iron Ingots to forge a full set or armor and tools, but if you want yo create a minecart rail network to between your base and your minning cave that's also gonna cost a significant ammout of ingots. And that's not even including stuff like buckets to collect lav and water, make a lighter, sears so you can carve pumpkins, trim sheep for wool and cut leave blocks from trees, ect.
After one trip to a mine I managed to get out with 50 Iron ores I could make into Ingots, If I make myself a set of Iron armor and tools my supply of Iron is almost nearly gone.

Copper allows you to have armor and tools significantly better than Leather armor or Stone tools AND allows you yo save your Iron for when you actually need it.

Am I seriously alone on this?

The Inventory Problem™️

Since this is a hot topic among the community and keeps coming up in discussion regarding new updates, I wanted to drop in my two cents since these points usually get buried under piles of complaints and plain counterpoints that complaints are entitled.
# The core issue

The raw number of different items and blocks has expanded significantly and will keep doing so, no way around it. While back in the day, an inventory of 36 slots was enough to carry just about everything you'd ever need realistically, this has changed.
Undeniably, the amount of items multiplied immensely since these days, build styles have emerged that were not a thing back then, build palettes have become more complex. Mobs drop more stuff, not on a per-mob basis but the overall variety of drops. Environments have more ambient plants and various doodads. Redstone requires more and more specialized components.

Of course this is a good thing. It's a natural consequence of the game being alive and well.
It does mean however that things that used to be quick and easy to do have become more cumbersome. And solving this will always have to be compatible with both Java and Bedrock, all supported deviced and all the supported input methods from touch through gamepad to mouse/keyboard and beyond.
# The suggested change

> Just increase the inventory, that'd fix everything

Lots of people usually request this not seeing that, no, it wouldn't fix everything. And Mojang know this.

Increasing the inventory has a couple of issues that people like to overlook. It's fighting inflating numbers with inflating other numbers.
We already established that the raw number of items in this game will continue to grow. This is inevitable. This means if increasing the inventory is the fix, the player's inventory will become unwieldy. People will complain that they can't find in their inventories what they need to access. Depending on the client they might need to scroll. The next request will be tabbed inventory, a bigger hotbar, more hotbars, bigger stack sizes, ...
Players will have to juggle more and more types of tools, weapons, blocks, decoration, redstone components, whatever depending on what they're doing at the moment. Controlling a cursor with a gamepad across a huge grid of items could become troublesome, especially if it has to happen quickly.
# Mojang's approach

Mojang is already tackling this problem in very smart ways and people often dismiss these approaches, thinking each one of them is supposed to solve "the" inventory problem while each solves "a" inventory issue and collectively they will solve it sustainably.

A quick recap on what we have right now:

  * 2013: Donkeys and Mules have the ability to carry chests, effectively increasing the player's inventory on land by 15 slots.
  * 2016: Shulker Boxes allow the player to carry chests with their whole inventory, 27 additional slots in a single slot. Llamas also offer the ability to carry chests, but in contrast to donkeys and mules, they have the caravan mechanic which means up to nine llamas in sum can increase a player's inventory on land by 135 slots.
  * 2019: The barrel is a slightly cheaper storage option, the stonecutter reduces the number of items you usually need to transport while building. Campfires allow cooking food without using the inventory.

  * 2022: Chest Boats are added, increasing the inventory on water by 27 slots. Allays offer a new option for handling items in specific situations without needing to spend time in the inventory. While this was a community vote, the choice to offer the allay was very much concious on Mojang's side.
  * 2023: The decorated pot and the chiseled bookshelf also reduce the amount the player actually spends in their inventory when using certain items.

  * 2024: The crafter again reduces the amount the player actually is required to handle stuff in their inventory manually. Bundles allow stacking multiple, up to 64, different items in a single slot.
  * 2025: Leads allow transport of multiple chest mobs and chest boats at the same time, immensely increasing the player's effective inventory. Copper Golems were conciously picked up from a past vote by Mojang, and explicitly changed from their former mechanic to a new behaviour which, again, offers to reduce the time a player is required to spend in their inventory.
Shelves allow swapping up to 9 inventory slots at once without even opening the inventory, streamlining the handling of items and tools immensely.
# Observations

Especially in the more recent years, it's incredibly obvious that Mojang know perfectly well that inventory and item handling are a very complex problem that need a series of parallel approaches to solve them reliably for good.

They apparently try to follow multiple philosophies at the same time:

  * In general reduce the time the player needs to spend in the inventory at all

  * Make handling items in specific situations more streamlined
  * Increase the inventory in specific situations with trade-offs
And this is a way smarter approach than just increasing the inventory flat out. If done well, reducing the time in the inventory means players are less likely to run into situations where the inventory becomes a problem at all. Streamlining handling items means situations where the inventory has become a problem are quicker and easier to deal with.
Increasing the inventory with trade-offs then allows for niche situations to offer a bonus while asking the player to actually engage with the game's mechanics.
# The future

From these observations we can make a few fair estimations as to where we're headed.

  * Increased inventory while travelling across lava. I think Striders carrying chests is too obvious, but some kind of other lavaborne, swimming mob that can carry a few chests while being slower than the Strider seems likely to me.
  * A more streamlined way to specifically handle only tools and weapons inside the inventory. Some kind of toolbelt that allows to stack multiple tools into one slot and allows switching between them without needing to open the inventory.

  * Switching of the currently equipped armor quickly. This might be done as an update to the armor stand or as a new block that works like the powered shelf and allows for switching the currently equipped whole armor set with the stored one.
  * A palette item storing a variety of dyes for using multiple dyes without handling them in the inventory manually.
  * More direct interactions with blocks for specialized storage. I could see specialized record racks for storing stacks of record discs, some kind of pantry for holding food items, storing an arbitrary amount of one color dye in a paint bucket block, potion racks, specialized storage for ores, ingots, seeds, among others. These will most likely be handling a single type of item with huge variations or a lot of different items that all work the same way.
  * A way to simply replace a block or transform it in its location. Examples would be a smelting spell that transforms a block into its furnace output at a cost or cuts blank stone into bricks or logs into planks. Maybe something that allows the transformation of any already placed wood product into a different wood.
In my opinion, we are actually likely to see a couple of these across the next couple of years. If a simple increased inventory comes at all, it will probably come at a cost. A backpack that gives a single extra row of 9 slots at the cost of not being able to wear armor is a common suggestion that seems realistic to me. But I don't think this will actually be that necessary long term, if the already established philosophies are followed and implemented to their full potential.
Solving the situations where the inventory frustration actually comes up is way more useful than delaying the problem a couple updates into the future.

When your favorite game no longer feels the same.

I’ve been playing Minecraft for almost 13 years now. In that time, I’ve played over 1,500 hours across PC, console, and legacy console editions, and i absolutely loved it.
I’ve always enjoyed taking my time in a new world, but I rarely progress very far. Even after playing on a world for nearly a month, the furthest I usually get is building a cozy compound, enchanting diamond tools, and setting up a mob farm.

There’s still so much content I want to experience but just haven’t yet. I’ve never properly explored the Nether, done an ocean monument, ancient city, trial chambers, or even fought the Ender Dragon, for example.
Lately, though, something feels different. I’ll start a new world, mine some stone, build a house, make a farm but within just a few hours my enjoyment crashes through the ground. I end up quitting and deleting the world, and then start over the next day. It repeats over and over and over again. I don’t know why it’s happening… and I hate it.

How would you "fix" the inventory problem?

It's common knowledge that, since its release, many many items and block variants have been added to the game without the same attention being given to storage space.

While bundles were a neat addition for early game clutter, they don't really help with mass storage, which is where the core of the issue lies.

^{Also, I'm sure many mods address this issue in their own way, but not everybody has access to play with mods.}
What would you like to see or what ideas do you have in mind that could go toward helping fix this problem, which many players identify as (one of) the game's biggest ongoing problem(s)?

Personally, I think a backpack item could go a long way.
It would take the chest slot, add a player inventory worth of space, and there would still be balance in that you'd have to choose between a backpack, a chestplate, or elytra. In my mind, you can take it off and put it down anywhere similar to a shulker box, however you can't carry it in your inventory or nest it inside another container.
Another item could be, leather pants with pockets. Again, you'd have to choose between the pockets of the leather (or even wool pants, or some kind of fabric) and better protection armour.
Additionally, maybe some kind of feature you can 'attach' to a chest (either put an item in it, or ideally 'tap/tag' it with an item) that lets you clone and access the same chest from multiple places. Similar to an ender chest but instead of one universal inventory for all ender chests, it's linking two specific chests, and then you can do that multiple times (either/both: cloning the same chest multiple times, and/or multiple pairs of cloned chests).
It could give you two items to begin with so you can 'tag' two chests - the second would have to be empty, since it would just become a clone of the first.

Then if you want to clone it beyond those two, you can duplicate it like the netherite upgrade.

You'd have to gather the resources and craft an item (probably magic item, maybe from a new end biome or what have you). So they could balance it in their own way.

I'd love to hear other folks' thoughts and ideas on this topic!
And thanks for reading if you did! Take care ~

I came up with an idea on how to overhaul the enchanting system to make it more fun

I was playing minecraft and reseting a librarian with a lectern for like 2 hours yesterday and it made me realise just how bad the enchanting system was, so I decided to brainstorm ideas on how Mojang could fix it (and therefore make enchantments like Mending more satisfying to obtain). It still needs some tweaking but here's the overall idea.
It's been clear for years now that the minecraft progression is flawed, especially with systems like enchanting or brewing that never felt rewarding. My idea is to separate all enchantments into 3 different categories (Offensive, Defensive and Misc./Utility), and create 3 different skill trees with each of them. I also thought that separating the enchantment levels to slow down progression could be a good idea although it might make the system too grindy depending on the price of each tree node.
I believe the player should be forced to unlock some of the lesser used enchantments like Smite or BoA (at least in earlier parts of the tree) so that they're forced to engage with them because IMO they are underrated and underutilised. Mostly because it takes the same amount of effort to get sharpness 5 as it takes to get BoA 5 but the actual enchantments aren't equal in power.
The way the player would unlock these enchantments would be by spending a set amount of levels (with some enchantments being more expensive). Important side note - Mojang would need to make levels equal, as you may or may not know, currently leveling up from 0 to 1 takes WAYYYY less XP than from 100 to 101 despite both of these being "one level". The player would then be allowed to put chosen enchantments on the piece of gear they want to enchant.
such action would cost an amount of lapis depending on how many different enchantments the player would choose (a nice way to repurpose lapis within the reworked system). I also thought about the bookshelves, obviously they're so iconic they can't go away.
Bookshelves should be truly optional instead of a requirement, my idea is that each 3 bookshelves around the enchanting table would bring down the lapis price by 7.5% rounded up (I was thinking lapis price should vary between 10 - 90 so a 37.5% decrese in price would feel fair). Additionally it would bring down the level price of unlocking enchantments by (1/2/3) levels on (5/10/15) bookshelves respectively. Finally the books, make them mid to late game loot and take the stronger books away from villagers.
Books should be obtainable from Bastion chests, End city chests, Ancient city chests or as Trial chamber loot etc.
Overall this is what I came up with to fix the unfun nature of traditional minecraft enchanting, as a big terraria fan it makes me sad to see that both sandbox block games have a terrible enchantment system that is neither engaging or fun. Maybe i'll target brewing next if this post gets positive feedback. Feel free to share your opinion and more importantly counter-ideas / constructive criticism. Thank you for attention and see you in the next one. :*

We added a no mending rule on the server....but:

So last year me and my mates started a server, plain vanilla, a few vanilla tweaks, just smp. We added one rule though: NO MENDING. We realised from previous servers we mine once for diamonds and that's it. Once we had mending we didn't have to anymore, same with getting the elytra, once you have a few with mending you never had to go to the end anymore. So we decided to challenge ourselves by banning mending.
Since then we made one exception for the Trident as it's the only breakable that can only be repaired with another trident and not with some item. Since the trident is more of a gimmick it doesn't change the overall rule that much.
I have to say it's different playing like this as you sometimes have big plans but when you're tools and armor are to expensive to repair you have to hold off on your plans and go back to the roots a little and I like that.

Now the but... Since we have this rule, no one has netherite or armourtrims as it's too expensive to dupe (the trims) and repair (the netherite) and not worth the trouble since it will break eventually.
We are a year in the server and have made big progress but some of us are starting to doubt the rule, what would you do in my situation? Commit to the rule or abolish it as one year of it was enough.

Toughts?
EDIT: if anyone has a datapack that allows the too expensive cap to be removed, without removing the level scaling (for example: the 15th time repairing your pickaxe it takes 87 levels) it would make our rule a little more playable. Also maybe a datapack to make it you can repair netherite with diamonds or scrap? DM me if you have something like this.

The update that Minecraft needs:

Minecraft is in dire need of a quality-of-life improvements, polish, bug fixing update. I think they've been lacking in these areas for too long. Right off the bat, Hytale already has Minecraft beat in some of these areas. I suggest many of the following be added:

  * Torches light up the area when held

  * A button to sort inventory/chests

  * A button or hotkey to unload items to nearby chests if they match existing items.
  * Crafting will see and use items from nearby storage

  * Focus on more bug fixing, especially old ones that have been around for years

  * Performance optimisation

  * Better multi-core utilisation

  * LOD (level of detail, like distant horizons or voxy, so we can see much farther)

  * Native support for connected textures in resource packs, maybe add some vanilla connected textures

  * Popup that shows what you're looking at (like the "what am I looking at" mods)

  * Better animations
  * Holding food shows how much it replenishes (like the apple skin mod)

  * Native support for shader packs, also the vanilla shader should add some improvements such as shadows, moving water, reflecting water, waving grass/leaves etc. (all optional)

  * Add a dynamic wind system (varying strength and direction, affects the waving leaves and water, and falling direction of entities, toggleable in settings)

  * More gradual and realistic weather transitions
  * Sound physics and better ambient sounds (echoes in caves and valleys, wind on hilltops and plains)

  * Water splashes when entities fall into water

  * Enchantment for hoes that harvests a larger area

  * Enchantment for hoes that plows a larger area

  * Enchantment for hoes that auto-replants seeds

  * Enchantment for axes that auto-replants saplings

Should Minecraft Have More Bosses Apart From Ender Dragon?

I've just finished watching a vid about guy beating Minecraft with 0 knowledge about the game (rue is the channel on YT)

I wish he'd seen more of the game, but beating it actually feels like an end. I always felt like that and assume he feels something similar — there is no point in exploring and finding all those peculiar structures if I've finished the game
So I thought: what if Minecraft had more bosses apart from the Ender Dragon? You'd need to find different rare items, to open the portal/tomb/whatever to fight a different hard boss and get the unique loot

That would make:

  1. "Beating the Game" more non-linear

  2. Give meaning to all the "unnecessary" structures like ancient city, jungle pyramids, mansions, and especially ocean monuments

  3. Motivate to keep playing and exploring even after beating you first boss
Potentially it could make beating the Dragon less meaningful, and turn into something repetitive, like a "to-do list". I just want those places to make sense. Ocean monuments, for instance, look very interesting, but there is no point in going in there in terms of progression or loot

Mojang added the Sift to introduce future bosses to the game.

Fighting a boss became one of the most memorable moments in Minecraft following the addition of the wither and the ender dragon, both of which represents the nether and the end respectively. There is also the elder guardian in the overworld, despite being significantly weaker than the two, and the warden (which I talk more about below).
With each dimension already having a unique boss, I believe one of the problems Mojang has encountered is that they cannot add any more bosses in the game that will feel distinct or coherent to the already existing dimensions.

The overworld should feel neutral, with the exception of hostile mobs that are relatively easy to deal with. The end hosts the ender dragon which I think should remain the last and only boss of the dimension. Adding another boss will  only lower its presence and uniqueness.
Adding a new boss to the nether is an option, but the design must remain true to the hellish atmosphere of the dimension, limiting the space for new and interesting ideas; And I think the Wither already acts as the ultimate boss of the nether similar to the ender dragon.
With the addition of the sift, Mojang now has the excuse to add new bosses to the game. We've seen that the sift is full of souls and (I think) that these souls are able to manifest into distorted versions of life forms, which gives Mojang more space to create interesting boss designs that may otherwise conflict with the design of the other dimensions.
An example is the warden, which is the sole representative of the previously unknown dimension. It is one of the most unique mobs Mojang has added to the game, with it being the only boss to be introduced before its dimension. With its unique design and approach to combat, I am certain that Mojang intended the warden as a teaser on how they are willing to break previously established design conventions for the new mobs that will be added in the game.
